newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firm, Brent near day's high.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firm, Brent near day's high.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended up to $3 a tonne firmer on Thursday amid continued pre-winter heating oil buying on both sides of the Atlantic.
November Brent crude futures stood up 35 cents at $23.45 by 1717 GMT after hitting a session high of $23.50.
November gas oil closed at $234.50, up $3 and not far from Thursday's high of $235.
A cold blast in the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest heating oil consumer, sparked nervous buying as U.S. distillate stocks stand 29 percent below 1995 levels.
Heating oil demand in the northeastern U.S. is expected to be above normal in the next few days as temperatures run 5-10 degrees Farenheit below normal, meteorologists said.
Gas oil prices in Europe and the U.S. are running at post-Gulf War highs.
"People are looking at the low stock situation and are severly worried about what will happen when winter hits," a broker said.
The November Brent-gas oil crack spread, indicating gas oil's relative strength, ended gas oil trading at the day's high of $8.07.
